numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When the power equation has no solution (e.g. a one-sided test whose effect_size points into the wrong tail), the root finder fails to converge, success is set to 0 and a ConvergenceWarning is emitted, but solve_power still returns val, the last point the solver evaluated (a bracket bound), e.g. array([10.]) for TTestPower().solve_power(effect_size=0.5, alpha=0.05, power=0.8, alternative="smaller"), which looks like a valid sample size.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Return nan when the solver fails to converge (success flag 0), signalling that no solution was found; cases that currently converge are unchanged and cache_fit_res still records the raw solver output.
trigger_conditions: Power equation has no solution, e.g. one-sided test with effect_size pointing into the wrong tail (such as alternative="smaller" with positive effect_size)
Root finder fails to converge so success is 0 and ConvergenceWarning is issued
Caller does not treat the ConvergenceWarning as fatal

input_output_examples.buggy_output: ConvergenceWarning: Failed to converge on a solution. array([10.])
input_output_examples.source: pr_body:PR#9884 (Problem section); expected nan per commit message and test test_solve_power_no_solution_returns_nan

oracle_clues: Regression test test_solve_power_no_solution_returns_nan asserts the two sign-mismatched one-sided cases return nan with a ConvergenceWarning and cache_fit_res[0] == 0
A solvable control case must still return a finite value
Verified red-green: test fails on main returning array([10.]) and passes with fix
Full test_power.py and test_gof.py suites pass

category_specific_evidence: solve_power in statsmodels/stats/power.py returned val, the last point the root solver evaluated (a bracket bound), after the solver failed to converge; the fix sets val = np.nan when the success flag indicates failure (success != 1), keyed off the existing success flag so only runs that already failed to converge are affected

Reproduction case: TTestPower().solve_power(effect_size=0.5, alpha=0.05, power=0.8, alternative="smaller") emits ConvergenceWarning and previously returned array([10.]) (lower bracket bound) instead of nan
Failure mode: power equation has no solution (one-sided test with effect_size pointing into the wrong tail); no nobs satisfies target power, so root finder does not converge
Mirror case: alternative="larger" with effect_size=-0.5 is also impossible and should return nan with ConvergenceWarning
Control case: alternative="larger" with effect_size=0.5 is solvable and must return a finite sample size
cache_fit_res[0] == 0 on failure, and cache_fit_res still records raw solver output for debugging
Regression test test_solve_power_no_solution_returns_nan in statsmodels/stats/tests/test_power.py asserts nan, ConvergenceWarning and cache_fit_res[0]==0 for failing cases
Iteration count, initialisation of the solver, and exact stopping tolerance of the root finder are not stated in the passages
reproduction_risks: Passages do not state the root finder's initialisation, stopping criterion, tolerance or iteration count, so the convergence-specific properties requested cannot be filled from evidence
Returned value of array([10.]) is a bracket bound that depends on the solver's search bounds, which are not specified in the passages
Fix returns nan rather than raising; a caller who does not check for nan may still propagate it
Sign-check up-front interception of impossible cases was left as a follow-up, so impossible inputs still reach the root finder
